  "confidence": 0.5,
  "anomalies": [
    {
      "category": "bridged_nets",
      "components": ["Module1", "U21", "J4", "U20"],
      "pins": ["Module1.55", "U21.4", "J4.3", "U20.2"],
      "nets": ["TX_GPIO14"],
      "observed": "The net named TX_GPIO14 contains the CM4 GPIO14 pin (Module1 pin 55), the FT231XS RXD input (U21 pin 4), the J4 serial header pins 1 and 3, and also the 3.3 V rail: the LDO output U20 pin 2 (VO), U21 pin 13 (3V3OUT), and the VCC/VDD pins of U1, U5, U7, U15, U17, U18, U19, U22, U24, U31, U32, U33, U34, U35 and U36. A GPIO pin, a UART data input, and the regulated 3.3 V output are therefore electrically the same node.",
      "expected": "GPIO14 (UART TX) should be a separate signal net that reaches FT231XS RXD and J4 pin 3, not the +3V3 supply node. The 3.3 V rail should only connect to power pins and their decoupling.",
      "evidence": [
        {"source": "netlist", "quote": "(net (code \"196\") (name \"TX_GPIO14\") (class \"Default\")"},
        {"source": "netlist", "quote": "(node (ref \"Module1\") (pin \"55\") (pinfunction \"GPIO14\") (pintype \"passive\"))"},
        {"source": "netlist", "quote": "(node (ref \"U21\") (pin \"4\") (pinfunction \"RXD\") (pintype \"input\"))"},
        {"source": "netlist", "quote": "(node (ref \"U20\") (pin \"2\") (pinfunction \"VO\") (pintype \"power_out\"))"},
        {"source": "spice", "quote": "C29 +3V3 0 470uF"}
      ],
      "impact": "The CM4 UART TX output would be tied to the 3.3 V regulator node, so the debug serial path through the FT231XS and J4 would not work. The Pi's GPIO14 would fight the regulator output, and a fault could damage the GPIO or the LDO.",
      "confidence": 0.5
    },
    {
      "category": "wrong_value",
      "components": ["R36"],
      "pins": ["R36.1", "R36.2"],
      "nets": ["VOUTN", "VOUTP"],
      "observed": "R36 is valued \"24k\", but its library description says \"24Ω 0805 Chip Resistor\" and its MPN is FRC0805J240TSD, which denotes 24 Ω.",
      "expected": "The value field should match the orderable part. A 24 kΩ bleeder would need a 24k part, while the described 24 Ω part would load the VOUTP/VOUTN bank far more heavily.",
      "evidence": [
        {"source": "netlist", "quote": "(comp (ref \"R36\") (value \"24k\")"},
        {"source": "netlist", "quote": "(description \" 125mW Thick Film Resistors 150V ±100ppm/℃ ±5% 24Ω 0805 Chip Resistor - Surface Mount ROHS\")"},
        {"source": "netlist", "quote": "(field (name \"MPN\") \"FRC0805J240TSD\")"},
        {"source": "spice", "quote": "R36 VOUTN VOUTP 24k"}
      ],
      "impact": "If the 24 Ω part is fitted, the supercap bank discharges through a low resistance. If the 24 kΩ value is intended, the BOM and procurement data are wrong.",
      "confidence": 0.35
    },
    {
      "category": "open_connection",
      "components": ["D30", "R60"],
      "pins": ["D30.4", "D30.2", "R60.2", "R60.1"],
      "nets": ["ESTOP_OUT", "Net-(D30-K2)"],
      "observed": "The second LED channel of D30 has its anode pin A2 (pin 4) on ESTOP_OUT and its cathode K2 (pin 2) through R60 also on ESTOP_OUT. Both LED terminals therefore sit on the same net, so this channel can never conduct. The first channel, by contrast, has its anode on the LED supply net.",
      "expected": "The LED anode should be on a supply or drive net and the cathode through R60 to ESTOP_OUT, so that the indicator lights when ESTOP_OUT is pulled low.",
      "evidence": [
        {"source": "netlist", "quote": "(node (ref \"D30\") (pin \"4\") (pinfunction \"A2\") (pintype \"input\"))"},
        {"source": "netlist", "quote": "(node (ref \"R60\") (pin \"2\") (pintype \"passive\"))"},
        {"source": "spice", "quote": "R60 Net-_D30-K2_ ESTOP_OUT 130"}
      ],
      "impact": "The E-stop status LED channel never illuminates, so the operator loses an indication of the E-stop state. R60 carries no current.",
      "confidence": 0.25
    }
  ],
  "summary": "The most likely anomaly is the TX_GPIO14 net, which merges the GPIO14 UART TX line with the +3V3 regulator node and so shorts a GPIO to the supply. Lower-confidence findings are a 24k value on R36 whose description and MPN say 24 Ω, and an LED channel in D30 with both terminals on ESTOP_OUT."
}

anomalies.observed: The net named TX_GPIO14 contains the CM4 GPIO14 pin (Module1 pin 55), the FT231XS RXD input (U21 pin 4), the J4 serial header pins 1 and 3, and also the 3.3 V rail: the LDO output U20 pin 2 (VO), U21 pin 13 (3V3OUT), and the VCC/VDD pins of U1, U5, U7, U15, U17, U18, U19, U22, U24, U31, U32, U33, U34, U35 and U36. A GPIO pin, a UART data input, and the regulated 3.3 V output are therefore electrically the same node.
anomalies.expected: GPIO14 (UART TX) should be a separate signal net that reaches FT231XS RXD and J4 pin 3, not the +3V3 supply node. The 3.3 V rail should only connect to power pins and their decoupling.
anomalies.impact: The CM4 UART TX output would be tied to the 3.3 V regulator node, so the debug serial path through the FT231XS and J4 would not work. The Pi's GPIO14 would fight the regulator output, and a fault could damage the GPIO or the LDO.

anomalies.observed: R36 is valued "24k", but its library description says "24Ω 0805 Chip Resistor" and its MPN is FRC0805J240TSD, which denotes 24 Ω.
anomalies.expected: The value field should match the orderable part. A 24 kΩ bleeder would need a 24k part, while the described 24 Ω part would load the VOUTP/VOUTN bank far more heavily.

evidence.quote: (description " 125mW Thick Film Resistors 150V ±100ppm/℃ ±5% 24Ω 0805 Chip Resistor - Surface Mount ROHS")

anomalies.impact: If the 24 Ω part is fitted, the supercap bank discharges through a low resistance. If the 24 kΩ value is intended, the BOM and procurement data are wrong.

anomalies.observed: The second LED channel of D30 has its anode pin A2 (pin 4) on ESTOP_OUT and its cathode K2 (pin 2) through R60 also on ESTOP_OUT. Both LED terminals therefore sit on the same net, so this channel can never conduct. The first channel, by contrast, has its anode on the LED supply net.
anomalies.expected: The LED anode should be on a supply or drive net and the cathode through R60 to ESTOP_OUT, so that the indicator lights when ESTOP_OUT is pulled low.
anomalies.impact: The E-stop status LED channel never illuminates, so the operator loses an indication of the E-stop state. R60 carries no current.

parsed.summary: The most likely anomaly is the TX_GPIO14 net, which merges the GPIO14 UART TX line with the +3V3 regulator node and so shorts a GPIO to the supply. Lower-confidence findings are a 24k value on R36 whose description and MPN say 24 Ω, and an LED channel in D30 with both terminals on ESTOP_OUT.
